newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends above $23, but traders cautious.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends above $23, but traders cautious.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures surge through $23 a barrel in late trade on Thursday continuing a bounce started on Wednesday, but while fundamentals continue to point the market higher traders remained cautious over today's gains.
The March Brent contract last traded 40 cents a barrel firmer at $23.17 a barrel, just seven cents off the intra-day high.

Traders said the short term market took heart from the front month's holding of psychological support at $22 earlier in the week with the upside reinforced by stronger products and a tight North Sea spot market on Thursday, but few see it making $24.
Dealers said there was a more bullish tone to the market, but said it would need more news before it could push higher.
Brent and NYMEX WTI both shrugged off comments made earlier by U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan that he expected the oil-for-food deal with Iraq to be renewed for a further six months.
Traders said they did not expect any falls from the Iraq news with Iraqi oil already factored into the market again.
"The market knows that Iraqi oil is back." one trader said.
February gas oil futures last traded $7.75 higher at the intra-day high of $212.25 a tonne boosted by strong heating oil on NYMEX.
Bullish U.S. distillate inventory data on Wednesday and forecasts for colder weather in the U.S. Northeast were the main driving factors, traders said.

"I think it's just a continuation of yesterday helped by the cold weather in the States," one broker said. Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp saw below average temperatures in the key heating market of the U.S. Northeast over the next few days, increasing heating needs. Temperatures in Northwest Europe were also forecast to be slightly below normal for the rest of the week. -- Colin Wooster London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
